events.incident:
Two reports came in for the orders_api service:
1. Users say GET /orders/9/total sometimes returns 500.
2. A security reviewer suspects users can see other users' orders.

Test credentials for the sandbox: 'token-alice' (user 1) and 'token-bob' (user 2), sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'.

events.claim: GET /orders/9/total returns 500 intermittently due to unhandled exception in total calculation (e.g., coupon/discount edge case)
events.next_check: Read code for total endpoint, check logs, reproduce with requests

events.claim: Order retrieval endpoints lack ownership check, allowing any authenticated user to see other users' orders
events.symptom: users can see other users' orders
events.next_check: Read auth/order code and test cross-user access with token-alice vs token-bob

events.claim: GET /orders/9/total returns 500 intermittently due to unhandled exception in total calculation (e.g., coupon/discount edge case)
events.next_check: Read code for total endpoint, check logs, reproduce with requests
evidence: orders_api/app.py:39 order 9 has coupon None
orders_api/app.py:101 compute_total does order["coupon"]["percent"] without None check
log r-105 GET /orders/9/total 500 TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable at compute_total line 101
log r-109 same 500
log r-bf369025 same 500
reproduced GET /orders/9/total as token-bob -> 500 Internal Server Error
tests/test_orders.py::test_total_without_coupon expects 200 total 120.0 for order 9
events.reason: Order 9 has coupon=None, compute_total unconditionally subscripts coupon, causing TypeError and 500 on every /orders/9/total call; other orders succeed, explaining 'sometimes'

events.claim: Order retrieval endpoints lack ownership check, allowing any authenticated user to see other users' orders
events.symptom: users can see other users' orders
events.next_check: Read auth/order code and test cross-user access with token-alice vs token-bob
evidence: orders_api/app.py:93-96 read_order returns order with no owner check, vs lines 108-109 read_order_total does owner check
log r-106 GET /orders/7 user_id 2 status 200 though order 7 owner_id 1
log r-107 GET /orders/8 user_id 2 status 200 though order 8 owner_id 1
reproduced GET /orders/7 as token-bob -> 200 with Alice's order
reproduced GET /orders/9 as token-alice -> 200 with Bob's order
tests/test_orders.py::test_user_cannot_read_someone_elses_order expects 404 for Bob reading order 7
events.reason: read_order lacks ownership enforcement, so any authenticated user can read any order; confirmed by logs and live cross-user reads

report.incident:
Two reports came in for the orders_api service:
1. Users say GET /orders/9/total sometimes returns 500.
2. A security reviewer suspects users can see other users' orders.

Test credentials for the sandbox: 'token-alice' (user 1) and 'token-bob' (user 2), sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'.

hypotheses.claim: GET /orders/9/total returns 500 intermittently due to unhandled exception in total calculation (e.g., coupon/discount edge case)
hypotheses.next_check: Read code for total endpoint, check logs, reproduce with requests
evidence: orders_api/app.py:39 order 9 has coupon None
orders_api/app.py:101 compute_total does order["coupon"]["percent"] without None check
log r-105 GET /orders/9/total 500 TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable at compute_total line 101
log r-109 same 500
log r-bf369025 same 500
reproduced GET /orders/9/total as token-bob -> 500 Internal Server Error
tests/test_orders.py::test_total_without_coupon expects 200 total 120.0 for order 9
hypotheses.reason: Order 9 has coupon=None, compute_total unconditionally subscripts coupon, causing TypeError and 500 on every /orders/9/total call; other orders succeed, explaining 'sometimes'

hypotheses.claim: Order retrieval endpoints lack ownership check, allowing any authenticated user to see other users' orders
hypotheses.symptom: users can see other users' orders
hypotheses.next_check: Read auth/order code and test cross-user access with token-alice vs token-bob
evidence: orders_api/app.py:93-96 read_order returns order with no owner check, vs lines 108-109 read_order_total does owner check
log r-106 GET /orders/7 user_id 2 status 200 though order 7 owner_id 1
log r-107 GET /orders/8 user_id 2 status 200 though order 8 owner_id 1
reproduced GET /orders/7 as token-bob -> 200 with Alice's order
reproduced GET /orders/9 as token-alice -> 200 with Bob's order
tests/test_orders.py::test_user_cannot_read_someone_elses_order expects 404 for Bob reading order 7
hypotheses.reason: read_order lacks ownership enforcement, so any authenticated user can read any order; confirmed by logs and live cross-user reads

evidence: orders_api/app.py:39 order 9 has coupon None
orders_api/app.py:101 compute_total does order["coupon"]["percent"] without None check
log r-105 GET /orders/9/total 500 TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable at compute_total line 101
log r-109 same 500
log r-bf369025 same 500
reproduced GET /orders/9/total as token-bob -> 500 Internal Server Error
tests/test_orders.py::test_total_without_coupon expects 200 total 120.0 for order 9
issues.fix: Handle missing coupon in compute_total via order.get("coupon") or {} and .get("percent", 0) so total falls back to plain subtotal.
issues.root_cause: compute_total unconditionally did order["coupon"]["percent"]; order 9 has coupon=None, causing TypeError and 500. Other orders have coupons, explaining 'sometimes'.
issues.title: GET /orders/9/total returns 500 when coupon is None

evidence: orders_api/app.py:93-96 read_order returns order with no owner check, vs lines 108-109 read_order_total does owner check
log r-106 GET /orders/7 user_id 2 status 200 though order 7 owner_id 1
log r-107 GET /orders/8 user_id 2 status 200 though order 8 owner_id 1
reproduced GET /orders/7 as token-bob -> 200 with Alice's order
reproduced GET /orders/9 as token-alice -> 200 with Bob's order
tests/test_orders.py::test_user_cannot_read_someone_elses_order expects 404 for Bob reading order 7
issues.fix: Added ownership check in read_order: if order["owner_id"] != user["id"] raise 404, matching read_order_total behavior.
issues.root_cause: read_order lacked ownership enforcement, so any authenticated user could read any order (IDOR), confirmed by logs and live cross-user reads.
issues.title: IDOR: any authenticated user can read any order via GET /orders/{id}

findings.summary: Confirmed and fixed both reports: None-coupon crash on /orders/9/total and missing authz on GET /orders/{id}. Verified with 5 passing tests, no regressions.
